newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seeks stronger Spratlys code of conduct.
newsitem.headline: Manila seeks stronger Spratlys code of conduct.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday called for the strengthening of the code of conduct between China and the Philippines that calls for restraint in the disputed Spratly Islands in the South China Sea.
Ramos said he made the suggestion in talks with visiting Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian, and Chi agreed with him.
Philippine Defence Secretary Renato de Villa, who attended the meeting, earlier told reporters Ramos did not discuss the Spratlys territorial dispute with the Chinese official.

Ramos told his weekly news conference he suggested to the two defence ministers "that perhaps they could enhance the language of the code conduct...and the defence minister responded very favourably".

Ramos did not say what changes he wanted in the code, which calls on both countries to refrain from any provocative action that would disrupt peace in the Spratlys, a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals.
The area is claimed wholly or in part by China, the Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.

Despite speculation about the deteriorating health of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, Chi was not cutting short his Manila visit and would proceed to Jakarta on Thursday, Philippine officials said.
"I had a very good discussion with President Ramos. We should carry our friendship for generations," Chi said, speaking through an interpreter.
Chi later on Wednesday witnessed the signing of an agreement for China to provide Philippine army engineers with Chinese dump trucks worth $3 million.
